subject: ela
cluster: Range of reading and level of text complexity

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'To make lemonade, you will need lemons, water, and sugar. First, squeeze the juice from the lemons into a pitcher. Next, add water and sugar. Stir well until the sugar dissolves. Finally, add ice and enjoy!'

What type of informational text is this? Name two clues from the text that tell you the type.
items.answer: This is a how-to text (procedural text). Two clues: (1) it lists materials needed (lemons, water, sugar), and (2) it uses order words like 'first,' 'next,' and 'finally' to give steps in sequence.

steps: Read the text and look for structure clues.
Clue 1: lists materials at the start (lemons, water, sugar).
Clue 2: uses 'first,' 'next,' 'finally' to show steps in order.
Both clues are features of how-to (procedural) texts.
How-to texts always give steps in order and list what you need.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Malala Yousafzai grew up in Pakistan where girls were sometimes not allowed to go to school. She spoke out bravely for girls' education. In 2012, she was shot for speaking out, but she survived. She went on to win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, becoming the youngest winner ever.'

This is a biography. What is the main point the author wants you to understand about Malala? Use two details from the passage.
items.answer: The main point is that Malala showed great courage in fighting for girls' education. Detail 1: she spoke out even when it was dangerous, and was shot for it. Detail 2: her bravery was recognized when she became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize winner at age 17.

steps: A biography tells the story of a real person's life.
What is the main message about Malala? Her courage and fight for education.
Detail 1: she was shot for speaking out but continued.
Detail 2: she won the Nobel Peace Prize as the youngest winner ever.
Both details support the idea that she showed exceptional courage.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Plastic bags are destroying ocean wildlife. Over eight million tons of plastic enter the ocean each year. Turtles and seabirds mistake plastic for food and die from eating it. We must ban single-use plastic bags now. The ocean cannot wait any longer.'

What type of informational text is this? What is the author's purpose? Name one reason the author gives.
items.answer: This is a persuasive text. The author's purpose is to convince readers to ban single-use plastic bags. One reason given is that turtles and seabirds mistake plastic for food and die from eating it.

steps: Look for clues about text type: 'We must ban...The ocean cannot wait.' These are calls to action.
A text that tries to convince the reader to do something is persuasive.
Author's purpose: convince readers to ban plastic bags.
One reason: turtles and seabirds eat plastic by mistake and die.
Persuasive texts have a call to action AND reasons to support it.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'The Venus flytrap is a plant that eats insects. When an insect touches the hairs inside its leaves, the leaves snap shut in less than a second. The plant then releases juices that digest the insect over several days.'

Explain the cause-and-effect chain in this passage. What triggers the trap? What happens next?
items.answer: The cause-and-effect chain: (1) An insect touches the hairs inside the leaves (cause). (2) The leaves snap shut in less than a second (effect/new cause). (3) The plant releases juices to digest the insect over several days (final effect). Each event leads to the next.

steps: Identify the trigger: insect touches the hairs.
First effect: leaves snap shut in less than one second.
Second effect: plant releases digestive juices.
Third effect: insect is digested over several days.
This is a cause-and-effect chain: each event is both an effect and the cause of the next.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean, completing the flight in 1932. She dreamed of flying from a young age and practiced at every opportunity. In 1937, she disappeared while trying to fly around the world. Her bravery and skill inspired generations of pilots.'

The passage says Earhart 'inspired generations of pilots.' What evidence in the passage supports this claim?
items.answer: The evidence is that she was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean and attempted to fly around the world. These achievements were historic firsts that showed other pilots, especially women, what was possible. The passage also says she had bravery and skill, which are qualities others would admire and want to follow.

steps: The claim: she inspired generations of pilots.
What evidence supports this?
Evidence 1: first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic. This was historic.
Evidence 2: attempted to fly around the world (no one had done it solo before).
Evidence 3: the passage says 'bravery and skill' which are inspiring qualities.
Historic firsts by a brave, skilled pilot would naturally inspire others.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'The giant panda eats almost nothing but bamboo, consuming up to 40 pounds per day. Bamboo is not very nutritious, so pandas must eat nearly all day to get enough energy. Giant pandas are endangered because their bamboo forest habitats are being destroyed.'

What connection does the passage make between bamboo and pandas being endangered?
items.answer: The connection is: pandas need bamboo forests to survive (they eat bamboo all day for energy). When bamboo forests are destroyed, pandas lose their only food source and habitat. So destroying bamboo forests directly threatens pandas' survival.

steps: Pandas eat almost only bamboo, up to 40 pounds per day.
Bamboo is not nutritious, so they must eat nearly all day.
Pandas are endangered because bamboo forest habitats are being destroyed.
Connection: if bamboo forests are gone, pandas have no food and no home.
The passage implies: loss of bamboo = loss of pandas.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'You should learn to write cursive handwriting. Cursive is faster than printing once you learn it. It also helps you read historical documents and old letters that are written in cursive. Finally, studies suggest that writing by hand strengthens memory.'

This is a persuasive text. What makes you sure it is persuasive and not just informational? What is the strongest reason given?
items.answer: It is persuasive because the first sentence says 'you SHOULD learn cursive,' which is a recommendation, not just a fact. An informational text would describe cursive without telling you to do anything. The strongest reason is probably that it helps you read historical documents, because this is a practical skill with lasting value that purely learning to print cannot provide.

steps: Clue 1: 'You should learn...' is a recommendation. Informational texts do not tell you what to do.
Clue 2: all three reasons are given to support the recommendation.
To identify persuasive text: look for 'should,' 'must,' 'need to,' or calls to action.
Strongest reason: reading historical documents is a unique, lasting benefit.
Faster writing and memory are also good reasons but more general.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Mangrove trees grow along coastlines in warm places. Their tangled roots protect the shoreline from waves and storms. Fish and crabs use the roots as nurseries, hiding there until they are big enough to survive in the open ocean. When mangroves are cut down, coastal communities suffer more damage from storms.'

What is the main idea? How do all four sentences work together to support it?
items.answer: The main idea is that mangrove trees are important and valuable ecosystems. Sentence 1 establishes where they grow. Sentence 2 shows how they protect coastlines. Sentence 3 shows how they support ocean wildlife. Sentence 4 shows what happens when they are gone (storm damage). All four sentences together show different aspects of mangrove importance, building the main idea from multiple angles.

steps: Main idea: mangroves are important ecosystems.
Sentence 1: sets the scene (where they grow).
Sentence 2: shows a protective role (coastline from waves).
Sentence 3: shows an ecological role (nursery for fish and crabs).
Sentence 4: shows the consequence of losing them (storm damage).
Each sentence adds a new dimension of importance.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'The Northern Lights, or Aurora Borealis, appear as colorful waves of light in the night sky near the North Pole. They are caused by charged particles from the sun interacting with gases in Earth's atmosphere. The lights can be green, pink, blue, or red.'

A student reads this and says, 'This must be made up because lights don't just appear in the sky.' How would you use the text to show the student this is a real phenomenon?
items.answer: I would point to the scientific explanation in the text: the Northern Lights are caused by charged particles from the sun interacting with gases in Earth's atmosphere. This is a scientific cause-and-effect explanation, not a made-up story. Informational texts give real, scientific explanations, which is what this text does.

steps: The student thinks it is made up because it sounds impossible.
Find the scientific explanation: charged particles from the sun + Earth's atmosphere gases = lights.
This is a cause-and-effect explanation based on science.
Made-up stories do not explain causes using scientific terms like 'charged particles' and 'atmosphere.'
The text is informational because it gives a verifiable scientific cause.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'To build a simple birdhouse, you will need wood, nails, and a hammer. First, cut four pieces of wood for the walls. Nail the walls together. Add a roof on top. Drill a small hole in the front for the birds to enter. Hang the birdhouse from a tree branch.'

Identify the text type and explain two features that make it this type. Then explain why the order of the steps matters.
items.answer: This is a how-to text. Feature 1: it lists materials needed at the start (wood, nails, hammer). Feature 2: it uses sequential order (First... then implied steps in order). Order matters because some steps depend on earlier steps: you cannot hang the birdhouse before nailing the walls, and you cannot drill the entry hole before having walls to drill into.

steps: Text type: how-to. Features: materials list, step-by-step order.
Feature 1: materials listed at start.
Feature 2: steps in sequence starting with 'First.'
Why does order matter?
You must have walls before adding a roof.
You must have a structure before drilling a hole.
You must complete the birdhouse before hanging it.
Doing steps out of order would make the task impossible or produce a faulty result.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Wilma Rudolph was born premature and had polio as a child, which left her unable to walk normally for years. Doctors said she would never walk unaided. With determination and daily exercise, she not only walked but became a runner. In 1960, she won three gold medals at the Olympic Games and became the fastest woman in the world.'

How does the structure of this biography build toward its main point?
items.answer: The biography starts with Wilma's greatest obstacles (being born premature, having polio, doctors saying she could not walk). It then shows her overcoming them (determination, daily exercise, learning to walk). It ends with her greatest achievement (three Olympic gold medals, fastest woman in the world). This structure of challenge to triumph makes the final achievement feel even more remarkable.

steps: Sentence 1: challenge (premature birth, polio, unable to walk).
Sentence 2: obstacle (doctors said she could never walk).
Sentence 3: overcoming (determination, exercise, walking then running).
Sentence 4: triumph (three Olympic gold medals, fastest woman).
Structure: problem to solution to triumph.
Starting with obstacles makes the final achievement more impressive.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Schools should serve healthier lunch options. Currently, many school lunches contain too much sugar and salt. Children who eat healthy food concentrate better and get sick less often. Investing in healthy school meals is investing in students' futures.'

Identify the text type. Then explain what each sentence does: does it state the point, give a reason, give evidence, or make a call to action?
items.answer: This is a persuasive text. Sentence 1: states the point (schools should serve healthier lunches). Sentence 2: gives evidence of the current problem (too much sugar and salt). Sentence 3: gives a reason (healthy food helps children concentrate and stay healthy). Sentence 4: makes a broader call to action by framing it as an investment in the future.

steps: Text type: persuasive. Clue: 'Schools SHOULD serve...' is a recommendation.
Sentence 1: the main point/claim.
Sentence 2: evidence (current lunches have too much sugar and salt).
Sentence 3: reason (healthy food improves concentration and reduces illness).
Sentence 4: call to action framed as an investment.
Persuasive texts typically contain: point + evidence + reasons + call to action.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'The ocean is divided into five zones based on depth. The sunlight zone is at the top where light reaches and plants grow. Below that is the twilight zone where there is very little light. The midnight zone, the abyss, and the hadal zone below that have no sunlight at all and are extremely cold.'

What is the main idea of this passage? How does the author organize the information, and why does that organization work well for this topic?
items.answer: The main idea is that the ocean is divided into depth zones with different light and temperature conditions. The author organizes the information from top to bottom, starting with the sunlit surface and moving to the deepest, darkest zones. This top-to-bottom organization works well because it mirrors how you would physically travel downward through the ocean, making the zones easy to follow in order.

steps: Main idea: ocean has zones based on depth.
Organization: the author moves from top (sunlight zone) to bottom (hadal zone).
Why does this work? Because the topic is about depth, and depth is naturally ordered top to bottom.
The structure matches the physical reality of the ocean.
Organizing information in a way that mirrors the real-world structure makes it easier to understand.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Katherine Johnson was a mathematician who worked for NASA. She calculated the flight paths that allowed astronauts to travel to space and return safely. Her work helped make the first moon landing in 1969 possible. Without her calculations, the mission could have failed.'

A student says: 'This biography just lists things she did. There is no main point.' Do you agree? What is the main point?
items.answer: I disagree. The main point is that Katherine Johnson's mathematical work was essential to NASA's success and to human space exploration. The details are not just a list; they build toward the last sentence ('Without her calculations, the mission could have failed'), which reveals the main point: her work was not just important, it was irreplaceable.

steps: Is there a main point beyond just listing facts?
Look at the last sentence: 'Without her calculations, the mission could have failed.'
This is the most powerful statement. It shows her work was critical.
The other sentences build to this conclusion.
Main point: Johnson's mathematical genius was essential and irreplaceable to NASA.
The student missed the main point because they did not read the last sentence as a conclusion.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

'Deep-sea fish live in complete darkness miles below the ocean surface. Many have developed their own light, called bioluminescence, which they use to attract prey or find mates. The anglerfish has a glowing lure that dangles from its head. Small fish swim toward the light, not knowing they are heading toward a predator.'

What is the main idea? Then explain how the last two sentences act as an example that supports the main idea rather than adding a new idea.
items.answer: The main idea is that deep-sea fish have developed bioluminescence (their own light) to survive in total darkness. The last two sentences describe the anglerfish using its glowing lure to hunt. This is an example of the main idea, not a new idea: it shows specifically how one fish uses bioluminescence to attract prey, which is one of the uses mentioned in sentence 2. The example makes the main idea concrete and vivid.

steps: Main idea: deep-sea fish produce their own light (bioluminescence) to survive in darkness.
Sentence 3: anglerfish has a glowing lure on its head.
Sentence 4: small fish swim toward the lure and are caught.
Is this a new idea? No. The main idea says bioluminescence is used to attract prey.
The anglerfish example shows exactly that: using a lure (light) to attract and catch prey.
An example supports a main idea by making it specific and real.
